answer.rationale: Current write path latency is 5x target during peak settlement traffic. A security patch that must not be reverted was deployed 2 hours ago, eliminating rollback as an option. Memory_b5 demonstrates that routing read queries to replicas can reduce primary load and recover transactional latency same-day. Memory_b3 shows that provisioning/load-shifting before peak absorption works—here we apply the same principle by offloading non-transactional reads. This preserves writes, respects the compliance constraint, and has proven precedent. Regional failover risks moving peak load between regions without addressing root cause. Circuit breakers protect downstream but don't resolve the write latency itself. Add capacity takes time we don't have. Routing read replicas is the fastest, lowest-risk intervention to recover write latency while keeping the security patch in place.
